clue.text: Share gin, dropping in, with girl, posh

parts.note: a cut is a share of the takings

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so the named letters are let go from the word before

explanation.surface: Someone well-bred splits the gin with a young woman who has just dropped by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping in' reads as visiting, but it tells you to take IN out of GIN, leaving G.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-glass accent is a precise, upper-class way of speaking, so the adjective serves as a synonym for posh.

clue.text: Sea fish heading for Canadian river

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the Usk is a river in Wales

explanation.surface: A saltwater fish is swimming towards a river in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: The cusk, or torsk, is a cod-like fish of the North Atlantic, so it is a kind of sea fish.

clue.text: Unpaid, has translated Sanskrit treatise

indicators.note: translating turns text into a different form, so these letters come out rearranged

explanation.surface: An unpaid scholar has translated an ancient Indian text.
explanation.definitionFit: The Upanishads are philosophical treatises in Sanskrit that form part of the Hindu Vedic scriptures.

clue.text: Turn over and force up stone

parts.note: T/O is the business abbreviation for turnover

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to zap is to hit with force

explanation.surface: Instructions for prising a rock loose: flip it, then lever it upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests lifting a heavy stone; 'stone' is in fact the gem being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Topaz is a precious gemstone, and jewellers call any gem a stone.

clue.text: Carriage going between Switzerland and Austria

indicators.note: only the stretch that goes across the gap between the two country names is kept; everything further out is dropped

parts.note: the country's name with its first seven letters dropped
the country's name cut to its first two letters

explanation.surface: A coach travels on the road between two Alpine countries.
explanation.walkthrough: In effect a hidden word: the letters straddling the border of the two names join up once you skip the 'and' set between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding hood at each end.

clue.text: Fish famously we ignored on Cyprus not allowing rays to penetrate?

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so the pronoun is taken away

parts.note: Michael Fish was a well-known BBC weather forecaster

explanation.surface: Some famous fish was overlooked while we were in Cyprus, and the rays could not get through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' looks like an animal, but it is Michael Fish, the British TV weatherman famous for dismissing the 1987 hurricane.
explanation.definitionFit: Athermancy is the property of being impervious to radiant heat, so heat rays cannot pass through.

clue.text: Can it grate lemon drink?

parts.note: 'can it!' means be quiet, the same as sh

explanation.surface: A question asking whether a tin can be used to grate a lemony beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as being able to, but 'can it' is slang for shut up.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrub is an old drink made of fruit juice, often lemon or orange, sugar and rum or other spirits.

clue.text: Tales written and spoken? They'll start thus (often)

definitions.text: Tales written and spoken? They'll start thus (often)

indicators.note: where words start is their opening letter, so only the first of each is kept

explanation.surface: A remark that many stories, in print or told, begin the same way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the four opening words start with the very letters of the word that starts so many tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic contraction meaning 'it was' is the classic opening word of narrative poems and fireside stories.

clue.text: Tragic heroine about effected what marriage entails

indicators.note: about means around, so the heroine's name is wrapped round the other word

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles, Hardy's tragic heroine
to win is to bring about, achieve

explanation.surface: A doomed heroine brought about the union that marriage involves.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage joins two people, so it involves being a pair: the state of being two.

clue.text: Bark displays this texture

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the weft threads of a woven fabric

explanation.surface: Tree bark shows a certain grain.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'bark' as a tree's outer layer; the first meaning is a dog's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a dog's bark and the weft, the crosswise threads giving woven cloth its texture.

clue.text: Run through reeds growing wild round garden

indicators.note: round means placed all about, so the jumbled letters enclose the garden
plants that grow wild spread in no set order, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: Kew Gardens, the Royal Botanic Gardens in London

explanation.surface: Reeds running riot around a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To skewer is to pierce, so run through and skewered are synonyms as past participles.

clue.text: Chat idly with wife cutting meat? It's done clumsily

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so these letters go inside the meat
doing something idly means without care or order, so these letters are casually rearranged

explanation.surface: Gossiping idly while one's wife carves the joint, which is badly done.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchwork in a figurative sense means work that is clumsily cobbled together from bits.

clue.text: Drains setting health resorts back

indicators.note: setting something back means sending it the other way, here read from right to left
back means in the opposite direction, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Wastewater issues are hurting tourist spa towns.
explanation.definitionFit: To sap is to drain strength or energy, so saps and drains are verbs with the same sense.

clue.text: Something resembling flying boat adjusted panel aloft (10, two words)

indicators.note: adjusting changes how things are set, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aircraft-like craft has had a panel adjusted up in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A float plane is a seaplane with floats rather than a hull, so it resembles a flying boat.

clue.text: Praise for Scots flew aloft round ring

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the verb goes around the ring letter

explanation.surface: Praise from the Scots soared round a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Roose is a Scottish and dialect word meaning to praise or extol.

clue.text: Fish wrapped in thin round dumpling

indicators.note: wrapped in means enclosed by, so the fish goes inside
turned round means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fish wrapped in a thin round dumpling, like some ravioli.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin round' looks like a description of the dumpling, but round is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A knaidel is a matzo-meal ball served in soup in Jewish cookery, a type of dumpling.

clue.text: Signature tune: The Dancing Gnomes (9, two words)

indicators.note: dancers move about, so these letters are shuffled into new positions

explanation.surface: Reads like a title: the signature music of a show called The Dancing Gnomes.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme song is the tune that identifies a show or performer, which is what a signature tune is.

clue.text: I go round for something from the takeaway?

definitions.text: I go round for something from the takeaway?

parts.note: surface reading: someone going round to a shop for a takeaway meal
setter's reading: the speaker is the food itself, which comes round in shape

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I go round' as the dish speaking about itself: it is circular and goes out from the takeaway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian flat round bread with toppings is one of the commonest takeaway meals.

clue.text: Muscle stick-like, minimum of callisthenics admitted? Naughtiness

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so this letter goes inside the adjective
the minimum of a word is its smallest part, here just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Is a muscle thin as a stick, with little exercise taken? That is bad behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Peccancy is sinfulness or offence, from Latin peccare, to sin, so it is a formal word for naughtiness.

clue.text: Tree line (not to be overstepped)? Live within it

indicators.note: within it means inside the thing just named, so the verb goes inside

parts.note: the oche is the line a darts player must not cross when throwing
to be is to live, exist

explanation.surface: A tree marks a boundary not to be crossed; live inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: The oche is the throwing line in darts, a pub game popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeche is a West African tree yielding a light timber, so it is an example of a tree.

clue.text: One supplies eiderdown? Misshapen lumps arise

indicators.note: misshapen means distorted out of form, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone who sells duvets finds lumps forming in the stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eiderdown' suggests a quilt, but the question mark points to the feathers themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumassier is a dealer in ornamental feathers, so supplying eider down is a jokey example of the trade.

clue.text: The idle mucked about, oblivious to the Bard

indicators.note: mucking about means messing around, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Lazy people messing about, unaware of Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Bard' is Shakespeare; the definition is his word for causing forgetfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's 'Lethied' alludes to Lethe, the mythical river of forgetfulness, so it is his word for oblivious.

clue.text: Political economist turning flat in Messiah

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the other name
turning means facing about, so the word is read back to front

explanation.surface: A singer turns flat during a performance of Handel's Messiah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' suggests music or housing; here it means dull, insipid.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrematistics is the study of wealth, so a chrematist is a political economist.

clue.text: It records pics I take, wizard inside

indicators.note: inside means within, so the wizard sits between the other letters

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin 'take', on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A device for snapshots: I take one with a magician inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An imager is a device that produces images, such as a camera or scanner.

clue.text: Ordinary contralto accompanied by Rubinstein?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for contralto
Anton Rubinstein, Russian pianist and composer

explanation.surface: A plain contralto singer with a famous pianist on piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordinary' looks like an adjective for the singer, but in heraldry an ordinary is a simple charge on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a canton is a square in the upper corner of a shield, classed as one of the ordinaries.

clue.text: Moulding, two wings conjoined within circles

indicators.note: within means inside, so the paired wings sit between the circles

parts.note: in heraldry a vol is a pair of wings joined at the base

explanation.surface: A decorative moulding shows a pair of joined wings set in rings.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovolo is a convex rounded moulding in architecture, like a quarter circle.

clue.text: Stifled, dropping dead

explanation.surface: Smothered, someone falls down dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping dead' reads as collapsing; here 'dropping' is a noun, bird dung.
explanation.definitionFit: Muted means silenced or softened, so it is a synonym for stifled.

clue.text: Flowering plants perfect illuminated from below

indicators.note: in a down entry, read from below means read from the bottom up, so backwards

explanation.surface: Flowers look perfect when lit by lamps beneath them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilia is the genus of lime or linden trees, which bear fragrant flowers.

clue.text: Wheeze spattering Scotch, last in bottle

parts.note: jap is a Scots word for spatter, splash

indicators.note: the last in a word is its closing letter, the only one kept here

explanation.surface: A wheezing drinker splashes the last of the whisky in the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' suggests whisky, but it marks the verb as a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeze in British slang is a clever trick or joke, the same as a jape.

clue.text: Youth in tomb, one espousing taxonomic theory

indicators.note: in places the young man inside the burial chamber

parts.note: a cist is a prehistoric stone tomb

explanation.surface: A young man in a tomb turns out to be a believer in classification theory.
explanation.definitionFit: A cladist follows cladistics, which classifies organisms by shared ancestry.

clue.text: Old pains beginning to nag with little support around

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the support encloses the letter

parts.note: a tee is a small peg supporting a golf ball

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

explanation.surface: Old aches start to nag with not much support around.
explanation.definitionFit: Tene is an obsolete word for grief or sorrow, so it stands for old pains.

clue.text: Marsh tree, some sequoia, gnarled, twisted

indicators.note: twisted round means turned to face the other way, so read backwards
some means part of, so the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: letters running across the end of the tree and the start of the adjective

explanation.surface: A tree in a marsh, part sequoia, gnarled and twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: Ngaio Marsh was a New Zealand crime novelist; her first name is also a New Zealand tree, so 'Marsh tree' is a punning definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ngaio is a small New Zealand tree, and also the first name of the writer Ngaio Marsh.

clue.text: Unattached drifter, latitude restricted by adversary

indicators.note: restricted by means hemmed in, so the letter is enclosed by the enemy

explanation.surface: A footloose wanderer has their freedom curtailed by an enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: A floe is a sheet of floating ice detached from the main mass, drifting free.

clue.text: Fashionable hoods converted pile in the sticks

indicators.note: in places the reworked letters inside the sticks
converted means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Trendy hoodlums turned an old heap into something in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sticks' suggests the countryside, but here it simply means canes.
explanation.definitionFit: Capelines are light hoods, once a fashion item for women, so they are a type of stylish hood.

clue.text: Last to stay the course and displaying old-style go

indicators.note: last to each word means only the closing letter of each is kept

explanation.surface: The final finisher stays the course and shows an old-fashioned way of going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay the course' reads as a phrase, but each of the four words gives up only its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeed is a Spenserian form meaning to go, an archaic verb for travel.

clue.text: Development of op? Where eager readers want to be

definitions.text: Development of op? Where eager readers want to be

parts.note: surface reading: an operation or opus growing into something larger

parts.words: Where eager readers want to be
parts.note: setter's reading: the abbreviation spelled out, the place keen readers turn to next

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'op' as a short form to be spelled out in full; keen readers are always wanting to turn on to the next leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means on the following leaf of a book, which is where an engrossed reader longs to get to.
